Individual controls for preamp and power amp overdrive for vintage and modern sounds. Two different phase inverter styles. Vintage rock, hard rock and old school metal tones and more. Rock guitar tone has long been defined by overdriven tube amplifiers. Those tones have evolved over the years as amps were intentionally designed for more gain and a more focused overdriven sound. You want those tones all the time, but we all live in the real world. You head out to a gig not knowing how loud you can play, whether youre amp will be micd or how much of an amp you can even fit on the stage. Your practice space is tiny and even the drummer thinks you are too loud. And of course you need to practice without waking the neighbors on occasion. We get it. Weve been there too. The Variac Overdrive emulates both a hot-rodded tube preamp and a power amp with two phase inverter options. Chords sound huge, leads sing with clarity, and pinch harmonics come out with ease. The Variac Overdrive is an expressive overdrive pedal with the articulation and touch sensitivity of a tube amplifier. The controls are interactive along with hidden controls like the power supply. Dynamics and headroom are all affected by the power supply. Powering from 7.5 to 18 VDC opens up even more possibilities. More on the hidden controls below. With tones ranging from AC/DC, early Van Halen, Judas Priest to Tom Morello and even 80s hair sounds, the Variac Overdrive is more than another amp in a box. It places an entire era of rock tone at your feet. Its based on tests of individual tube circuits, careful listening to some of our favorite rock and old school metal, and the topology of amplifiers the artists actually used. The “Hidden Controls”: These are not internal switches or knobs. No these are hidden plain sight. Playing loud makes a big difference. A big part of guitar tone is simply turning up to the point where the interaction between volume in the room makes notes sustain, harmonics bloom and simply sounding on the edge of being out of control. The Variac Overdrive is designed to react like an amp when its loud. Its a great pedal for practicing without waking the neighbors, but do yourself a favor and turn it up whenever you can. The power supply is an important part of a tube amplifier. It has a significant impact on The Variac Overdrive as well. It can be powered from 7.5 to 18VDC with wide changes in dynamics and compression. The sweet spot is usually about 8-15 volts, but will depend on your gear and playing style. Your guitar becomes and important part of the circuit too. SubDecay browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal SubDecay Variac Overdrive Published on June 11, 2014 SubDecay overdrive pedal prototype prototype Information The SubDecay Variac Overdrive is a dynamic overdrive pedal designed to recreate the sound and response of classic hot-rodded tube amplifiers. More than a simple "amp in a box," it models the behavior of both a tube preamp and a power amp stage, delivering a wide range of vintage rock, hard rock, and early metal tones. The pedal is engineered to capture the articulation, harmonic richness, and touch sensitivity of real tube circuits, allowing players to achieve tones reminiscent of late-1970s and 1980s rock icons such as AC/DC, Van Halen, and Judas Priest. Its dual gain structure provides independent control over preamp and power amp saturation, offering everything from low-gain crunch to full, saturated distortion. A two-position Cathodyne/LTP switch emulates different tube phase inverter topologies found in amplifiers: the Cathodyne setting produces a looser, bass-heavy response, while the LTP (Long Tail Pair) mode tightens the low end and adds focus for modern drive sounds. The pedal's EQ section, modeled after traditional tone stacks, allows separate adjustment of treble and bass frequencies. The Variac Overdrive also reacts to variations in power supply voltage, mimicking the "sag" and compression effects associated with tube amplifiers operating under variable conditions. Running the pedal between 7.5V and 18V DC changes its dynamic range and headroom, with a sweet spot typically between 8V and 15V. This voltage sensitivity, combined with interactive control behavior, gives the pedal an amp-like feel that responds naturally to playing intensity, guitar volume adjustments, and overall signal level. sources.bodyExcerpt: Suhr Eclipse — Grokipedia Search ⌘K Suggest Edit Sign in Sign in Overview Description Development and release Design Controls Channel configuration Voice control Connectivity and switching Technical specifications Sound characteristics Tonal capabilities Guitar applications Bass applications Reception Professional reviews User experiences References Fact-checked by Grok 7 months ago Suhr Eclipse Ara Eve Leo Sal 1x The Suhr Eclipse is a dual-channel analog overdrive/distortion effects pedal manufactured by Suhr Guitars (JS Technologies, Inc.). Released in 2017, it provides two independent channels—indicated by blue and red LEDs—each with identical circuitry featuring dedicated Gain, Level, and passive 3-band EQ controls (Bass, Middle, Treble) for precise tone shaping, along with a global Voice knob to adjust top-end brightness and match the pedal to different amplifiers. [1] [2] [3] The pedal is designed to deliver warm, organic, amp-like tones ranging from low-gain crunch and tube-style overdrive to high-gain saturated distortion, emulating the feel of a channel-switching tube amplifier in a compact stompbox format. [2] [1] Its architecture emphasizes versatility and dynamics, with each channel independently footswitchable and fully customizable, allowing users to configure contrasting sounds—such as a tight rhythm tone on one channel and a mid-forward lead on the other—without needing multiple pedals. A unique global Voice control fine-tunes high-frequency response to suit the amplifier's characteristics, while additional features include true bypass switching, FX Link connectivity for external control, and operation on 9-18V power (with low current draw and battery option). [2] [3] The Eclipse builds on the amp-in-a-box concept of Suhr's earlier Riot pedal (introduced in 2009) by offering expanded EQ flexibility and the Voice adjustment for broader tonal range and adaptability. [1] Primarily intended for electric guitar, the pedal excels at producing dynamic, responsive gain that retains clarity and touch sensitivity across various playing styles and rig setups. [3] [1] Overview Description The Suhr Eclipse is a dual-channel overdrive/distortion effects pedal manufactured by Suhr Guitars (JS Technologies, Inc., Lake Elsinore, California). [4] It is designed as a versatile, no-compromise drive pedal that delivers a wide range of warm, organic, amp-like tones in a compact and intuitive format. [4] [2] The pedal's core purpose is to provide guitarists with natural, dynamic saturation and responsive drive characteristics that emulate the feel and response of a cranked tube amplifier, while maintaining clarity and touch sensitivity across its gain range. [2] Its dual independent channels enable users to access contrasting tones—from low-gain overdrive to high-gain distortion—within a single pedal, offering flexibility for diverse playing styles and rig configurations. [4] [2] Development and release The Suhr Eclipse was developed and manufactured by JS Technologies, Inc., operating as Suhr Guitars, based in Lake Elsinore, California. [5] The pedal was introduced at the Winter NAMM Show in January 2017, with announcements and coverage appearing in mid-January of that year. [6] [7] It evolved from Suhr's single-channel Riot distortion pedal, first shipped in 2009, by incorporating dual independent channels to offer greater tonal flexibility while retaining the amp-like characteristics central to Suhr's pedal designs. [8] The Eclipse's release aligned with the industry's broader shift toward "amp in a box" overdrive and distortion pedals, which enable guitarists to achieve multi-channel, high-gain tones directly from clean amplifier platforms without requiring additional amp heads or complex setups. [7] Design Controls The Suhr Eclipse features two independent channels, each with identical controls for Gain, Level, and a 3-band passive EQ consisting of Bass, Middle, and Treble knobs. SIGNATURE TONE Kiko primarily uses his Shiba Drive as a boost to push the front-end of his amplifiers for increased sustain and harmonics. Based on feedback from Kiko we have modified the Shiba Re|Loaded circuit to offer greater clarity and low-end response while retaining the character and dynamics of the original. Available on: --> You may want these related items: DESCRIPTION VIDEOS In addition to the much loved Riot, we now also have the Suhr Riot RELOADED! First of all, the original Riot is NOT being replaced by the Riot Reloaded. They are two different pedals doing two different things. Sure, they're very similar, but certainly different nonetheless. The Suhr Riot has been very sucessful in finding it's way onto MANY pedalboards across the world since it's release in 2009. While still very much in demand in it's original form, Suhr realized there were many people that wanted a somewhat different variation of the Riot. By listening to customers' requests, the tone gurus at Suhr seeked to offer an alternate to the Riot that satisfied these requests. Through countless hours of testing and modifying, Suhr now offers the Riot in a versiona that is incrediably amp-like, aggressive, in your face, and features more gain (30% more than the original). Riot Reloaded is the ideal choice for players seeking Hi-Gain Rock, Metal, and drop tuning style tones. HOW DOES IT RESPOND? - One of the great things about playing a really nice amp is it's ability to respond to dynamics and touch. Most pedals have a difficult time with this, but the Riot Reloaded achieves this in a way few pedals can. Every nuance of your playing is brought out with it's extremely dynamic response. HOW MUCH GAIN? - The Riot Reloaded gives you over 30% more gain than the original. The engineers at Suhr balanced the dual gain stages to increase saturation and upper harmonics, resulting in improved midrange articulation, more sustain, and a tighter three-dimensional sound. With a simple twist of your volume knob, you can easily morph from mild chunk to full on metal assault. TONE SHAPING - The tone control was modified to emphasize upper mid frequencies for a sweeter, more cutting tone, without sounding harsh or fatiguing. QUICK FACTS: Amp-Like Dynamics and Response Over 30% More Gain than the original Modified Tone Control emphasizing upper mid frequencies for a more cutting tone. Three Position Voice Switch - Provides Classic, Modern, Scooped EQ settings. HOW ARE THE RIOT AND RIOT RELOADED DIFFERENT? 1) Essentially, the Riot is a bit more compressed with it's response while the Riot Reloaded offers more dynamics and a quicker response. 2) As well, the Tone control on the Reloaded is more of a Mid Frequency control as opposed to an All Frequencies tone control that is present on the Riot.
